Attempts.Response:
**Analysis:**

All three firewall profiles (Domain, Private, Public) report `Enabled : True`, which is the baseline requirement satisfied — no profile is turned off. However, `DefaultInboundAction`, `DefaultOutboundAction`, `AllowInboundRules`, and `AllowLocalFirewallRules` are all reported as `NotConfigured` rather than an explicit value on every profile, including Public. This is not the same as a confirmed safe state — "NotConfigured" means the effective policy depends on inherited GPO/local defaults that this output does not resolve, so it cannot be verified whether local rule creation is blocked or whether inbound traffic actually defaults to Block. Both `LogAllowed` and `LogBlocked` are `False` on all profiles, meaning no firewall event logging is occurring, which would hinder detection of blocked intrusion attempts or unexpected allowed connections.

Scanning the enabled inbound allow rules, none of them expose RDP, SMB, WinRM, or a database port by name — the list is dominated by discovery/casting/media protocols (mDNS, SSDP, WSD, DIAL, Wi-Fi Direct, Cast to Device, Delivery Optimization) plus several **Remote Assistance** rules (DCOM-In, RA Server TCP-In, TCP-In, PNRP-In, SSDP-In) that permit remote-control sessions and warrant scrutiny. Critically, this rule listing does not show per-rule profile scoping (Domain-only vs. also-Public) or `PolicyStoreSourceType`, so it is not possible from this output to confirm whether any of these rules — particularly Remote Assistance — are live on the Public profile, nor whether any were created locally outside GPO control.
